subject: integrating detection function in density surface models for a drone strip transect ?

messages.author: cb9340f365827f6d
messages.subject: integrating detection function in density surface models for a drone strip transect ?
parts:
We are in a bit of a pickle regarding how (and whether) we should apply the distance sampling framework on our drone imagery strip transects.  Is there a procedure within the distance sampling framework that can deal with detection not being 100 % inside a strip transect? Classic strip transects assume that all objects are detected in the covered area, which is far from the case with counts from our drone images. Analyzing the data in a ‘distance sampling’ framework with a uniform key function (no detection covariates allowed) is not ideal since detection is still not perfect due to background, image quality and solar angle (creating shadows) and such. We had seven independent observers going through the same imagery and observer detection of the “true” animals was in average 75 % (but varies depending on the covariates). The drone imagery is captured from a constant altitude so distance away from observer is the same on all imagery and thus distance from observer to animal does not influence detection.

The second alternative is to use a hurdle density surface model to get the abundance. We have been looking at the dshm_fit with ds() integrated but are running into the same problem. This function uses the same ds() function from the Distance package, thus would force us back to use uniform key function without covariates following the assumption of no detection error. How to integrate differences in detection probability between observers (for both P/A and count models) and possibly other covariates (e.g., image quality)?

So.. what is the best way to integrate detection in a density surface model when the drone strip transect violates distance sampling assumptions? Hoping for some useful suggestions as we are currently spinning our wheels a bit!

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] integrating detection function in density surface models for a drone strip transect ?
parts:
Hi Ingrid, hi listfolks,

I've spent a bit of time working on this but we've not finished that
particular analysis. So, I'm not sure if what I say below would equate
to anything like "the best way" to do it.

One way to approach this is to see the problem as not a distance
sampling one... in a DSM the detection function models the observation
process, then the GAM will deal with spatial effects. You can think of
your verification of the images as a kind of observation process in
itself, that you switch-out for the usual distance sampling model.

For example, in our case we had a mark-recapture observation process and
used the probability of capture in our DSM, then were able to propagate
uncertainty through the model for that. This required a fair amount of
custom coding to get things to work but it is doable.

If your observation process didn't depend on covariates, things would be
slightly easier as you'd simple be able to use your (say) 0.75 as an
offset in the model (the easiest way is to use the availability=...
argument) and fit things that way, then you can include uncertainty by
adding squared CVs, but if covariates are involved then adding the
squared CVs will leave out covariance between the observation and
spatial models (as it assumes independence between the processes). That
being said, that's probably not a bad starting point, then you can
consider fleshing the model out with a more complex observation process
model.

Hope that helps,
--dave
